t.1.60.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The six great seers are known as the mind-born sons of Brahman; and eleven sons of Sthāṇu are renowned, supremely mind-born.
t.1.60.2: Mṛgavyādha and Śarva, and the greatly renowned Nirṛti, Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, and Pinākī, scorcher of foes.
t.1.60.3: Dahana, and Īśvara too, and Kapālī of great splendor, Sthāṇu, and the blessed Bhava are known as the eleven Rudras.
t.1.60.4: Marīci, Aṅgiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu: these six mighty great seers are the sons of Brahmā.
t.1.60.5: Aṅgiras had three sons, renowned everywhere in the world: Bṛhaspati, Utathya, and Saṃvarta, all firm in their vows.
t.1.60.6: But of Atri, O lord of men, many sons are heard of, all of them great seers, knowers of the Vedas, perfected ones, of tranquil spirit.
t.1.60.7: The Rākṣasas, the Vānaras and likewise the Kiṃnaras are the offspring of Pulastya; of Pulaha are the deer, the lions, the tigers and likewise the Kiṃpuruṣas.
t.1.60.9: But Dakṣa, the blessed seer, the son of Brahmā and foremost among those blessed with sons, was born from his right thumb, O protector of the earth.
t.1.60.8: The sons of Kratu, equal to sacrifices, are companions of the sun; they are renowned in the three worlds and wholly devoted to truth and their vows.
t.1.60.10: From the left big toe of that great-souled one was born his wife; and in her that very sage begot fifty daughters.
t.1.60.12: He gave ten to Dharma, twenty-seven to Indu, and thirteen to Kaśyapa, O king, according to the divine rite.
t.1.60.11: As for those maidens, all of flawless limbs and lotus eyes, Prajāpati, whose sons were lost, established them as putrikās, appointed daughters.
t.1.60.13: Learn from me the wives of Dharma as they are named one by one: Kīrti, Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Medhā, Puṣṭi, Śraddhā, and Kriyā as well.
t.1.60.14: Buddhi, Lajjā and Mati: these are the ten wives of Dharma. These were ordained by Svayaṃbhū as the doors of Dharma.
t.1.60.16: The Grandfather is the divine sage; his son is Prajāpati. His sons are the eight Vasus; I shall tell of them in detail.
t.1.60.15: The twenty-seven wives of Soma are renowned in the world; these wives of Soma, of auspicious vows, are engaged in the measuring out of time. All of them are joined with the lunar mansions and are established in ordering the course of the world.
t.1.60.17: Dhara, Dhruva, Soma, Ahar, Anila, Anala, Pratyūṣa and Prabhāsa: these are known as the eight Vasus.
t.1.60.19: Ahar is the son of Ratā, and Hutāśana the son of Śāṇḍilī; Pratyūṣa and Prabhāsa are known as the two sons of Prabhātā.
t.1.60.18: Dhara was the son of Dhūmrā, and so was Dhruva, the knower of brahman; Candramas was the son of Manasvinī, and likewise Śvasana of Śvasā.
t.1.60.21: The son of Soma was Varcas, through whom one becomes radiant; and from Manoharā were born Śiśira, Prāṇa, and likewise Ramaṇa.
t.1.60.20: The son of Dhara was Draviṇa, and likewise Hutahavyavaha; the son of Dhruva was the blessed Kāla, who drives the worlds onward.
t.1.60.22: Jyotis is known as the son of Ahar, and likewise Śrama, Śānta, and Muni. The son of Agni is the glorious Kumāra, whose dwelling was a thicket of reeds.
t.1.60.24: The wife of Anila was Śivā; her son was Purojava, and also Avijñātagati. These two indeed were the sons of Anila.
t.1.60.23: His brothers were Śākha and Viśākha, and Naigameśa, born after him; and because the Kṛttikās came to him and nurtured him, he is known as Kārttikeya.
t.1.60.25: They know the seer named Devala as the son of Pratyūṣa. Devala, too, had two sons, both forbearing and wise.
t.1.60.27: The illustrious Viśvakarmā was born, the lord of the crafts, the maker of thousands of crafts and the carpenter of the thirty gods.
t.1.60.26: The sister of Bṛhaspati, an excellent woman devoted to celibacy and perfected in yoga, wanders through the whole world without attachment. She was the wife of Prabhāsa, the eighth of the Vasus.
t.1.60.28: He is the maker of all ornaments, the foremost of those skilled in the crafts, who fashioned the celestial chariots of the deities.
t.1.60.30: Splitting open the right breast of Brahmā, the blessed Dharma came forth in human form, bringer of happiness to all the worlds.
t.1.60.29: He is the great-souled one by whose craft men make their living, and whom they worship: the eternal, imperishable Viśvakarman.
t.1.60.32: Rati is the wife of Kāma, and Prāpti is the consort of Śama; Nandī is the wife of Harṣa, on whom the worlds are established.
t.1.60.31: He had three excellent sons, Śama, Kāma, and Harṣa, who captivated the hearts of all beings and who sustained the worlds by their splendor.
t.1.60.33: From Marīci came Kaśyapa, his son, and to Kaśyapa were born the Suras and Asuras, O tiger among kings; he indeed is the origin of the worlds.
t.1.60.34: Tvāṣṭrī, the wife of Savitṛ, that illustrious lady, assuming the form of a mare, gave birth in the sky to the two Aśvins.
t.1.60.35: Twelve indeed are the sons of Aditi, O lord of men, with Śakra foremost among them; the youngest of them is Viṣṇu, in whom the worlds are established.
t.1.60.36: These, then, are the thirty-three gods. I shall now relate to you their lineage, and their groups according to their divisions and their families.
t.1.60.38: The mighty Garuḍa, son of Vinatā, and likewise Aruṇa, and the blessed Bṛhaspati are counted among the Ādityas.
t.1.60.39: Know that the Guhyakas, all the plants, and likewise the animals come from the two Aśvins. This host of gods has been recited to you in due order, O king; by reciting it a man is freed from all sins.
t.1.60.37: Another group is that of the Rudras, and likewise of the Sādhyas and the Maruts; one should know the Bhārgava as belonging to the Vasus, and the Viśvedevas likewise.
t.1.60.40: Splitting open the heart of Brahmā, the blessed Bhṛgu came forth. Bhṛgu's son was the learned Kavi, and Kavi's son was Śukra, the planet.
t.1.60.41: Appointed by Svayambhū for the sake of sustaining the life of the three worlds, in rain and in drought, in danger and in safety, he courses all around the world.
t.1.60.42: A master of yoga and of great intelligence, he became the guru of the Daityas, and of the Suras as well, that wise brahmacārin, firm in his vows.
t.1.60.43: When that Bhārgava had been appointed by the Lord to secure the welfare and safety of the worlds, Bhṛgu begot another son, a blameless one.
t.1.60.45: Āruṣī, the daughter of Manu, was the wife of that wise man; in her was born Aurva of great fame, splitting open her thigh, a man of great austerity and great splendor, endowed with virtues even as a child.
t.1.60.46: Ṛcīka was his son, and from him Jamadagni was born. The great-souled Jamadagni had four sons.
t.1.60.44: Cyavana, of blazing austerity, righteous-souled and wise, who, O Bhārata, fell from the womb in anger to free his mother.
t.1.60.47: Rāma was the youngest of them, yet endowed with virtues that were not the least; skilled in all weapons and missiles, he was the destroyer of the kṣatriyas, and self-controlled.
t.1.60.48: Aurva had a hundred sons, with Jamadagni at their head; to them were born thousands of sons, and this was the spreading line of Bhṛgu.
t.1.60.49: Brahmā had two other sons, whose mark endures in the world: Dhātā and Vidhātā, who abide together with Manu.
t.1.60.50: Their sister was the goddess Lakṣmī, the auspicious one whose home is the lotus; and her mind-born sons were the horses that roam the sky.
t.1.60.52: From creatures craving food devouring one another, there arose Adharma, the destroyer of all beings.
t.1.60.51: The eldest wife of Varuṇa, a goddess, was born from Śukra; know Bala to be her son, and Surā too, the delight of the gods.
t.1.60.54: The goddess Tāmrā gave birth to Kākī, Śyenī, Bhāsī, Dhṛtarāṣṭrī, and also Śukī; these five are renowned throughout the worlds.
t.1.60.53: His wife too was Nirṛti, which is why the Rākṣasas are called Nairṛtas. She had three terrible sons, ever devoted to evil deeds: Bhaya, Mahābhaya, and Mṛtyu, the ender of beings.
t.1.60.56: Dhṛtarāṣṭrī, that radiant lady, gave birth to the haṃsas, the kalahaṃsas, and all the cakravākas, bless you.
t.1.60.55: Kākī gave birth to owls, Śyenī brought forth hawks, and Bhāsī bore bhāsa birds and vultures as well, O lord of men.
t.1.60.57: O knower of dharma, the high-minded Śukī, endowed with auspicious qualities and honored for all her marks, gave birth to parrots alone.
t.1.60.58: She also gave birth to nine Krodhavaśā women, born of her own self: Mṛgī and Mṛgamandā, Harī and Bhadramanā as well.
t.1.60.61: Then Bhadramanā gave birth to a son, the elephant Airāvata; Airāvata, her son, is the elephant of the gods, a mighty tusker.
t.1.60.60: The offspring of Mṛgī, O son of the best of men, are all the deer; and the offspring of Mṛgamandā are the bears, the sṛmaras, and the yaks as well.
t.1.60.62: And the offspring of Harī are the horses and the swift monkeys; and the golāṅgūlas too, bless you, they declare to be the sons of Harī.
t.1.60.59: Then Mātaṅgī, Śārdūlī, Śvetā and Surabhi as well, and the illustrious Surasā, endowed with every auspicious mark.
t.1.60.63: Then Śārdūlī gave birth to lions and tigers, O Bhārata, and to leopards as well, O fortunate one, to all of them without a doubt.
t.1.60.64: And the elephants, O lord of men, are the offspring of Mātaṅgī; and Śvetā bore the swift-moving elephant of the quarters named Śveta.
t.1.60.65: Likewise, O king, Surabhi gave birth to two daughters, Rohiṇī and the illustrious Gandharvī, blessings upon you. From Rohiṇī were born the cows, and from Gandharvī the horses as offspring.
t.1.60.67: Śyenī, the wife of Aruṇa, gave birth to two valiant sons of great strength, Saṃpāti and likewise Jaṭāyuṣa. The two sons of Vinatā, however, are the renowned Garuḍa and Aruṇa.
t.1.60.66: Surasā gave birth to the Nāgas, O king, and Kadrū to the serpents; Analā too brought forth the seven kinds of trees that bear round fruit. Śukī was the daughter of Analā, while Surasā was the daughter of Kadrū.
t.1.60.68: Thus, O lord of men, best of the wise, have I duly recounted to you the origin of all the great beings.
t.1.60.69: Having heard it properly, a man is purified of sin, attains omniscience, and reaches the highest state.
